question: Can an additive fixed-size C11 candidate allocator reproduce the existing Python producer's ordered validation, equal-share water filling and binary64 results, then compose through the existing native guard/pedal/clock/final gate without a Python allocator in that proposed path?
decision: Root reviewed the full proposal and owner source; bounded implementation approved with no semantic policy changes.

authority.owner: reference/allocator.py at the exact base, including pre-existing epsilon and status quirks
authority.numeric_contract: reference/torque_numeric.py version 2; fixed four-slot ordered binary64 accumulation
authority.acceptance: reference/allocation_contract.py plus existing real guard, trusted-pedal, cycle-clock, recovery and final-gate owners
authority.schema: AllocationInput and AllocatorConfig dataclasses, as constructed by bench_replay.py; dataclass annotations do not validate their fields

supported_domain.records: Ordinary AllocationInput/AllocatorConfig records and ordinary built-in JSON-style field values; no subclasses, conversion hooks, equality hooks, iterators or duck-typed arbitrary objects.
supported_domain.slots: Exactly four abstract slots; ordinary list/tuple shape is a decoder tag, with fixed C arrays. No confirmed physical wheel or motor mapping.
supported_domain.numeric_scalars: Ordinary Python int/float excluding bool, projected once to IEEE binary64 by the bridge. Finite converted values preserve bits; unrepresentable ints are malformed numeric tags. Float NaN/Inf remain numeric-tagged values so the request's nonfinite_request diagnosis is preserved. Limits classify every malformed/nonfinite/negative value as invalid_wheel_limit.
supported_domain.requested_result_projection: On successful Python paths requested_nm retains its original int/float object, unlike fault paths which normalize it. Direct parity compares float(requested_nm)'s binary64 bits, not Python integer identity, arbitrary integer precision or int-versus-float type. This is explicit normalized numeric result parity, not lossless JSON-integer serialization.
supported_domain.timestamps_and_age: Nonnegative ordinary integer no-wrap milliseconds in [0, UINT64_MAX]. A decoder-valid byte represents that exact subset; bool/fractional/negative/nonnumeric values become invalid tags. Python integers larger than UINT64_MAX are outside this supported C domain and the bridge must reject them as out of domain rather than claim an equivalent Python fault. No modulo rollover.
supported_domain.booleans: Only actual decoded Booleans map to bytes 0/1. Malformed source flags map to an invalid byte, never truthiness/coercion.
supported_domain.unit: Only the ordinary string N*m is supported. Reuse tc_text as a bounded representation; NONE, invalid/unterminated text, wrong strings, long strings and embedded NUL input are unsupported_torque_unit. A bridge may not turn a different source value into N*m. Source Python strings containing any embedded NUL MUST be encoded as invalid, never truncated to N*m. For raw valid C tc_text the first terminator defines its string; bytes after it are not original Python string identity and are ignored. No other port text semantics change.
supported_domain.floating_environment: Ordinary IEEE binary64 round-to-nearest with retained subnormals, nontrapping ordinary floating overflow and no reassociation/fast-math. Require sizeof(double)==8, radix 2, mantissa 53, exponent 1024 and FLT_EVAL_METHOD==0. Supported host GCC/Clang builds are checked empirically; no platform-universal or target-runtime claim follows.

proposed_additive_api.version: TC_ALLOCATOR_VERSION 1; existing TC_ABI_VERSION 1 and TC_NUMERIC_CONTRACT_VERSION 2 remain unchanged
proposed_additive_api.config: tc_allocator_config: uint8_t type_valid; uint8_t max_input_age_valid; uint64_t max_input_age_ms
proposed_additive_api.input: tc_allocator_input: uint8_t type_valid; uint8_t now_valid, timestamp_valid; uint64_t now_ms, input_timestamp_ms; tc_scalar request; uint8_t limits_vector_valid, enabled_vector_valid; tc_scalar limits[4]; uint8_t enabled[4], external_interlock; tc_text torque_unit
proposed_additive_api.output: Existing tc_allocation candidate only. Always initialize type_valid=1, wheel_vector_valid=1, every numeric tag=1, positive-zero wheel/delivered/request diagnostics, fault status and an explicit bounded diagnostic before validation. Successful raw proposals are not independently authorized commands.
functions: size_t tc_allocator_abi_sizeof(uint32_t kind): config=1, input=2, otherwise 0
uint32_t tc_allocate_propulsive_torque(const tc_allocator_input *input, const tc_allocator_config *config, tc_allocation *result)
proposed_additive_api.return_and_null: Return 0 for a fully initialized semantic result, including faults; return 1 for any required NULL. An available output is faulted/positive-zero before any other read. Output NULL cannot be written. Null failures use C-only missing_allocator_input diagnostics.
proposed_additive_api.outer_schema_order: After pointer checks, reject config.type_valid!=1 as C-only invalid_allocator_config_type, then input.type_valid!=1 as C-only invalid_allocator_input_type. These C-only paths retain requested=positive zero; Python cannot inspect these malformed outer objects reliably and direct result parity is not claimed for them.
proposed_additive_api.memory_preconditions: Complete aligned input/output objects, mutually non-overlapping storage; fixed arrays, no heap, no I/O, no scheduler or retained state. No alias/packed-wire ABI promise.
proposed_additive_api.decoder_obligations: Exactly 1 is a valid ordinary numeric/vector/record/time tag. Other bytes are malformed. Numeric tag 1 plus nonfinite double is a representable nonfinite float input, not an accepted finite value. Invalid Booleans must remain distinguishable from false. Adversarial direct ABI calls test all byte values.

exact_python_validation_order.check: max_input_age_ms is not ordinary int or is negative
request is bool or not an int/float; or ordinary integer conversion cannot produce a finite binary64
either vector is not list/tuple or either length is not four
any enabled flag is not an ordinary bool
external_interlock is not an ordinary bool
any limit cannot convert to finite binary64 or is < 0.0
either timestamp is not an ordinary nonnegative integer
now_ms - input_timestamp_ms > max_input_age_ms after the future check

exact_python_validation_order.result: ok, no fault, positive-zero wheels/requested/delivered; occurs before available-slot detection but after all earlier validation

exact_python_validation_order.check: otherwise execute the original ordered water filling
exact_python_validation_order.result: unmodified raw candidate, then external validation/guard/final gate in composed tests

fault_diagnostics: Every source-defined fault returns positive-zero wheels and delivered, status fault, the exact fault text, and finite converted request if available (including negative and negative-zero diagnostic bits), otherwise positive zero. This happens even when an earlier config/unit fault wins over a malformed request. No int-to-float exception escapes.

arithmetic_and_reduction_audit.no_hidden_sum: The full current allocator has no builtin sum/fsum, cap-sum prepass, compensation, fairness weights or weighted reduction. The active set is only a membership/count mechanism. A Python3.12 compensated builtin sum is therefore not an allocator operation to reproduce here.
arithmetic_and_reduction_audit.initialization: outputs=[+0.0]*4; remaining=converted request; epsilon is the binary64 value of literal 1e-12; active membership is enabled && converted_limit>0.0. Negative-zero limits are valid but unavailable.
arithmetic_and_reduction_audit.loop_condition: while active and remaining > epsilon; at most four rounds because each saturated round removes at least one active slot, while a nonsaturated round breaks immediately
arithmetic_and_reduction_audit.share: One binary64 division: remaining / len(active); active count is exact integer 1..4 converted to binary64. No division by zero.
arithmetic_and_reduction_audit.saturation_scan: Ascending slot index. For each active index, capacity=limits[index]-outputs[index] with binary64 rounding; compare capacity <= (share+epsilon) with a separate binary64 addition. Collect all qualifying slots before updating any remaining/output value.
arithmetic_and_reduction_audit.nonsaturated_branch: For every active index in ascending order, outputs[index]=outputs[index]+share; then set remaining=+0.0 and break. Do not substitute min, aggregate caps or a final balance slot.
arithmetic_and_reduction_audit.saturated_branch: For every collected slot in ascending order: capacity=max(+0.0, limits[index]-outputs[index]); outputs[index]=outputs[index]+capacity; remaining=remaining-capacity; remove this slot. Preserve each operation and rounding order; do not subtract a combined saturated-capacity sum.
arithmetic_and_reduction_audit.delivered: wheel_total(outputs) only: total=+0.0 then four separately rounded binary64 additions in slot order 0,1,2,3. This is the unchanged numeric contract 2. A private equivalent in the new C unit avoids changing the old contract unit's static helper/API/cohort.
arithmetic_and_reduction_audit.status: If final remaining > binary64 literal 1e-9, status saturated and fault aggregate_limit; otherwise status ok and fault NONE. No equality-to-request requirement is added.
arithmetic_and_reduction_audit.no_optimization_substitution: No sum(caps), request clipping, residual redistribution after the source stops, changing epsilons to relative/ULP tolerance, reordering slots, float32 conversion or numerical-policy update. Infinite sums of finite cap inputs are not an excuse to pre-sum capacities; preserve the source's actual loop.
arithmetic_and_reduction_audit.overflow_underflow: Do not assume every raw candidate from finite inputs satisfies the downstream acceptance contract. Preserve source arithmetic, including any nonfinite delivered total or epsilon over-request result encountered; direct parity records its exact result while composition must inhibit it via the existing validator/guard/gate. No downstream acceptance boundary is relaxed. The protocol does not predeclare whether a particular DBL_MAX fixture overflows; the unchanged Python owner supplies that result.

source_quirks_required_as_named_regressi: Request +0.0 and -0.0 produce fully positive-zero ok results only after all earlier validations; no available slot is needed for this exact zero path.
A positive request <=1e-12 with an available slot bypasses allocation and returns ok zero delivery; without available slots the earlier no_available_wheels fault wins.

One active slot, request=1.0 and limit=(1.0+1e-12 computed in binary64): threshold equality saturates to a cap above the request; raw status remains ok, while existing allocation_contract_fault/guard must reject candidate_exceeds_request and the composed command is positive zero.
A remaining positive shortfall between 1e-12 and 1e-9 can yield status ok when all slots are exhausted; source labeling must be retained, not relabeled saturated.
Ascending saturation removal can create rounding-sensitive remaining values. Mixed-magnitude caps, permutations and ULP-neighbor thresholds must preserve those exact operations.
Finite DBL_MAX requests and finite extreme caps: compare source outputs/total/status without pre-summing caps; include active counts 1,2,3,4 and invalid-result composition if it occurs.
DBL_TRUE_MIN/min-normal request and limits, signed zero limits, unavailable slots and exact epsilon/status boundaries remain source-compatible.
Negative finite requests, malformed flags/vectors, invalid config/unit and NaN/Inf/huge-int requests combine to test actual earliest-fault order and diagnostic request normalization.

planned_verification.oracle: Untouched actual allocate_propulsive_torque; direct normalized result signature compares four wheel double bits, delivered double bits, projected requested double bits, exact status and exact fault. Use binary64 hex/bit representations so signed zeros and nonfinite raw totals are representable in strict JSON receipts.
planned_verification.direct_grid: 18 requests x 16 fixed limit vectors x 16 enable masks =4608 direct cases, with a valid 50ms age policy and current timestamps. Requests: -0,+0,TRUE_MIN,MIN_NORMAL,1e-13,nextafter(1e-12,0),1e-12,nextafter(1e-12,+inf),2e-12,1e-9,nextafter(1e-9,+inf),1,nextafter(1,+inf),40,100,1e100,DBL_MAX/3,DBL_MAX. Limit vectors: all +0, all -0, all TRUE_MIN, all MIN_NORMAL, all 1e-12, all 1, all 20, all DBL_MAX; (4,20,20,20); (1,2,3,4) and reverse; (1e-12,1,1e100,DBL_MAX) and reverse; (1,0,0,0); (DBL_MAX,0,DBL_MAX,0); (DBL_MAX/3,DBL_MAX/3,DBL_MAX/3,0).
planned_verification.random_finite: 8192 seeded direct cases using seed 2026101508 and positive finite raw binary64 bit patterns for request and four caps, all 16 enable masks, with controlled current/age/future/no-wrap timestamp cases. No load generation beyond this finite comparison budget.
planned_verification.boundary_and_validation: Named quirks plus threshold neighbors, all active counts, malformed JSON-style fields, ordinary finite integer normalization, huge-int numeric rejection, every ordered mixed-fault pair, age boundary/future/UINT64_MAX cases and explicit out-of-domain bridge errors for larger timestamp integers. Cases and fixture generator hashes freeze before the first native verification run.
planned_verification.abi: All 256 tag values for each record/numeric/vector/time/text tag and enable/interlock flag; malformed/unterminated unit text; all three required NULL pointers; initialized result positive-zero behavior; version/sizeof checks. Malformed enable bytes >1 fault, but 0 is valid disabled and must not be treated as invalid. These C-only API checks are labeled separately from Python result parity.
planned_verification.full_composition: New additive five-unit host library: torque_contract.c, torque_clock.c, torque_pedal.c, torque_guard.c, torque_allocator.c. Actual proposed path uses C allocator output directly as the C guard candidate, then existing native pedal, clock and final gate. Existing decoder/adapters may normalize metadata; they must not substitute a Python allocator/guard output in the native path. Python owners supply the independent expected path only. Existing four-/three-unit builders and ARM experiment protocols remain unchanged.
planned_verification.stateful_streams: At least 1024 healthy/repeated/slew-limited cycles and 4096 recovery/trust/clock/restart cycles. Compare raw allocator, base/effective guard, clock fault AND full anchor, retained latch, proposed-output history, final gate state/streak/generation/reason and command bits. Assert actual positive accepted commands, held commands, limited accepted output, latch clearance, restart and clock-fault coverage. A coverage failure is a retained failed attempt, not a passing result with empty behavior coverage.
planned_verification.fail_closed_acceptance: Every held final vector is exact positive-zero bytes. Every allowed final vector matches the untouched Python pipeline and remains bounded by existing acceptance rules. A contradictory raw producer candidate is retained for direct parity but may never bypass the existing contract/guard/final gate.
planned_verification.determinism: Repeat the finite parity run twice on the same built library and compare result/case-count digests. Record exact compiler/version/argv, source and protocol hashes, ABI sizes, library hash, Python/runtime identity, seed, declared domain, denominators, pass/fail details and limits; retain failed attempts.
planned_verification.host_matrix: Run appropriate full local reference suite, then GCC/Clang x Python 3.11/3.12/3.13 host parity and Windows/Linux reference CI. Add a separate fifth actual ASAN/UBSan allocator probe in the existing sanitizer step; do not edit prior probe semantics. Actual sanitizer CI must pass before the new draft PR.
planned_verification.independent_review: After stable source/test/protocol/actual local parity receipt, independent adversarial review must inspect the producer arithmetic, all-tag/schema/null behavior and real stateful composition before publication. Findings and repairs remain explicit.
planned_verification.no_target_experiment: No ARM compiler/version/inspection calls, linking, target emulator/execution or hardware work in this increment. A future object annex needs its own separate protocol if useful. No GPU/model call needed.

primary_references.use: Python documents binary64 approximation and exact hexadecimal float interchange; this supports explicit normalized bit signatures, not a guarantee for arbitrary custom objects/platforms.
Compiler floating-point options motivate strict no-fast-math, no contraction and standard excess-precision flags; supported builds still require empirical parity.
C11 draft is the language reference for fixed types/operations and floating evaluation. C11 alone is not a promise of IEEE nearest/subnormal behavior; the narrower environment is explicit.

limitations: A faithful port preserves existing producer quirks; it is not a redesign or proof that every raw candidate is physically meaningful.
Equal allocation has no vehicle dynamics, traction/slip/yaw objective, weights, regeneration, calibration or physical motor mapping.
The orchestration remains offline Python and all data provenance remains caller-owned; normalized source fields are not verified sensor ownership.
No MCU runtime parity, firmware fit, complete-link/library behavior, real-time deadline/WCET, HIL, CAN, independent shutdown authority, vehicle actuation, course acceptance or safety certification.
No ARM compiler/object/link, GPU or hardware actions in this increment; implementation proceeds only from this separately frozen protocol.
